facts.text: A traffic lane is a section of road for a single line of traffic.

cites.quote: A traffic lane is a section of road for a single line of traffic.

facts.text: A single solid yellow line marks the center of a road with two-way traffic.

cites.quote: A single solid yellow line marks the center of a road with two-way traffic.

facts.text: Do not pass the vehicle ahead if there is only one lane going your direction and a solid yellow line is on your side of the road.

cites.quote: Do not pass a vehicle in front of you if there is only one lane of traffic going your direction and a solid yellow line on your side of the road.

facts.text: Do not pass over double solid yellow lines; stay to the right of them except in specific situations.

cites.quote: Do not pass over double solid yellow lines. Stay to the right of these lines unless you are:

facts.text: You may cross double solid yellow lines when you are in an HOV carpool lane that has a designated entrance on the left.

cites.quote: Stay to the right of these lines unless you are:
In a high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) carpool lane that has a designated entrance on the left.

facts.text: You may drive to the left of double solid yellow lines when construction or other signs tell you to use the other side because your side is closed or blocked.

cites.quote: Stay to the right of these lines unless you are:
Instructed by construction or other signs to drive on the other side of the road because your side is closed or blocked.

facts.text: You may turn left across a single set of double yellow lines to enter or exit a driveway or private road, or to make a U-turn.

cites.quote: Stay to the right of these lines unless you are:
Turning left across a single set of double yellow lines to enter or exit a driveway or private road or make a U-turn.

facts.text: Two sets of solid double yellow lines spaced two or more feet apart are a barrier: do not drive on or over it, or turn left or make a U-turn across it, except at designated openings.

cites.quote: Two sets of solid double yellow lines spaced two or more feet apart are considered a barrier. Do not drive on or over this barrier, make a left turn, or make a U-turn across it, except at designated openings.

facts.text: A broken yellow line next to your driving lane means you may pass, but only when it is safe.

cites.quote: A broken yellow line indicates you may pass if the broken line is next to your driving lane. Only pass when it is safe.

facts.text: A single solid white line marks traffic lanes going in the same direction, including on one-way streets.

cites.quote: A single solid white line marks traffic lanes going in the same direction. This includes one-way streets.

facts.text: Double solid white lines mark a barrier between a regular lane and a preferential lane such as a carpool (HOV) lane, and may also appear in or near freeway on and off ramps.

cites.quote: Double solid white lines indicate a lane barrier between a regular use and a preferential use lane, such as a carpool (HOV) lane. You may also see double solid white lines in or near freeway on and off ramps.

facts.text: Never change lanes over double solid white lines; wait until you see a single broken white line.

cites.quote: Never change lanes over double solid white lines. Wait until you see a single broken white line.

facts.text: Broken white lines separate traffic lanes on roads with two or more lanes going in the same direction.

cites.quote: Broken white lines separate traffic lanes on roads with two or more lanes in the same direction.

facts.text: Ending freeway and street lanes are usually marked with large broken lines; in such a lane, be prepared to exit the freeway or for the lane to end, and look for an exit or merge sign.

cites.quote: Ending freeway and street lanes are usually marked with large broken lines. If you are driving in a lane marked with broken lines, be prepared to exit the freeway or for the lane to end. Look for a sign that tells you to exit or merge.

facts.text: A yield line is a line of solid white triangles, pointing toward approaching vehicles, that shows where to yield or stop.

cites.quote: A yield line is a line of solid white triangles that shows approaching vehicles where to yield or stop. The triangles point towards approaching vehicles.

facts.text: The left (fast) lane is the Number 1 Lane; the lane to its right is the Number 2 Lane, then the Number 3 Lane, and so on.

cites.quote: The left (or fast) lane is called the Number 1 Lane. The lane to the right of the Number 1 Lane is called the Number 2 Lane. Then the Number 3 Lane, etc.

facts.text: Use the left lane to pass or turn left.

cites.quote: Use the left lane to pass or turn left.

facts.text: Use the right lane to enter or exit traffic, or when entering the road from a curb or shoulder.

cites.quote: Use the right lane to enter or exit traffic or when you enter the road from a curb or shoulder.

facts.text: Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and check traffic behind and beside you.

cites.quote: Before you change lanes:
Signal.
Check your mirrors.
Check traffic behind and beside you.

facts.text: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure the lane is clear.

cites.quote: Before you change lanes:
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure the lane is clear.

facts.text: Before changing lanes, check your blind spots for vehicles, motorcyclists, and bicyclists, and do not let your vehicle drift into another lane.

cites.quote: Before you change lanes:
Check your blind spots for other vehicles, motorcyclists, and bicyclists. Do not let the vehicle drift into another lane.

facts.text: Before changing lanes, make sure there is enough space for your vehicle in the next lane.

cites.quote: Before you change lanes:
Be sure there is enough space for your vehicle in the next lane.

facts.text: It is not necessary to slow down before a lane change.

cites.quote: It is not necessary to slow down before a lane change.

facts.text: Stay in one lane as much as possible and do not weave in and out of traffic; last-minute lane or direction changes may increase the risk of collisions.

cites.quote: Stay in one lane as much as possible. Do not weave in and out of traffic. Last minute lane or direction changes may increase the risk of collisions.

facts.text: Once you start moving through an intersection, keep going; if you start a turn, follow through.

cites.quote: Once you start moving through an intersection, keep going. If you start to make a turn, follow through.

facts.text: If you miss a turn, keep driving until you can safely and legally turn around.

cites.quote: If you miss a turn, keep driving until you can safely and legally turn around.

facts.text: On a multilane road, the passing lane is the far left lane, closest to the center divider, and is used to pass other vehicles.

cites.quote: On a multilane road, the passing lane (far left lane) is the lane closest to the center divider and is used to pass other vehicles.

facts.text: An HOV lane is a special lane reserved for carpools, buses, motorcycles, or low-emission vehicles with decals.

cites.quote: An HOV lane is a special lane reserved for carpools, buses, motorcycles, or low-emission vehicles with decals.

facts.text: You may use an HOV lane if you have the minimum number of people in your vehicle shown on signs at the on-ramp or along the road; signs also list the hours HOV rules apply.

cites.quote: To use an HOV lane, one of these must apply:

You have a certain number of people in your vehicle. There will be signs at the on-ramp or along the road to tell you the minimum number of people. Road signs also list the hours when the HOV rules apply.

facts.text: You may use an HOV lane in a low-emission or zero-emission vehicle if you display a special DMV-issued decal.

cites.quote: To use an HOV lane, one of these must apply:
You are driving a low emission or zero emission vehicle. You must display a special DMV-issued decal.

facts.text: Motorcycles may use HOV lanes unless otherwise posted.

cites.quote: To use an HOV lane, one of these must apply:
You are riding a motorcycle (unless otherwise posted).

facts.text: The road surface of an HOV lane is marked with a diamond symbol and the words Carpool Lane.

cites.quote: The road surface in a HOV lane is marked with a diamond symbol and the words Carpool Lane.

facts.text: Do not cross double solid lines to enter or exit an HOV lane; use the designated entrances and exits.

cites.quote: Do not cross over double solid lines to enter or exit an HOV lane. Use designated entrances and exits.

facts.text: A center left turn lane is in the middle of a two-way street and is marked on both sides by two painted lines: the inner line broken and the outer line solid.

cites.quote: A center left turn lane is located in the middle of a two-way street. It is marked on both sides by two painted lines. The inner line is broken and the outer line is solid.

facts.text: Use a center left turn lane only to prepare for and make a left turn or U-turn; it is not a regular traffic lane or a passing lane.

cites.quote: Use the center left turn lane to prepare for and make a left turn or U-turn. It is not a regular traffic lane or passing lane.

facts.text: You may drive no more than 200 feet in a center left turn lane.

cites.quote: You may only drive for 200 feet in the center left turn lane.

facts.text: Before turning left from a center left turn lane, look for vehicles coming toward you in the same lane.

cites.quote: To turn left from this lane:
Look for other vehicles coming toward you in the center left turn lane.

facts.text: To turn left from a center left turn lane, signal, look over your shoulder to check your blind spots, merge completely into the lane so you do not block traffic, and turn when it is safe.

cites.quote: To turn left from this lane:
Signal.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spots.
Merge completely into the center left turn lane so you do not block traffic.
Turn when it is safe.

facts.text: On two-lane roads with turnout areas or lanes, merge into them to let vehicles behind you pass.

cites.quote: Some two-lane roads have special turnout areas or lanes. Merge into these areas or lanes to allow cars behind you to pass.

facts.text: When driving slowly on a two-lane road where passing is unsafe and five or more vehicles are following you, you must use a turnout area or lane to let them pass.

cites.quote: You must use a turnout area or lane to let other vehicles pass when you are driving slowly on a two-lane road, where passing is unsafe, and there are five or more vehicles following you.

facts.text: Bicycle lanes are for bicyclists only, run alongside vehicle traffic, are typically marked by a single solid white line and signs, and are sometimes painted bright green.

cites.quote: Bicycle lanes are for bicyclists only and run alongside vehicle traffic. They are typically marked by a single solid white line and signs. They are sometimes painted bright green to make them easier to see.

facts.text: On a shared roadway, drivers must keep three feet of distance between their car and a bicyclist.

cites.quote: Three (3) feet of distance must be maintained between the car and cyclist.

facts.text: It is illegal to drive in a bicycle lane except to park where permitted, to enter or leave the road, or to turn within 200 feet of an intersection.

cites.quote: It is illegal to drive in a bicycle lane unless you are:
Parking (where permitted).
Entering or leaving the road.
Turning (within 200 feet of an intersection).

facts.text: A bike lane is typically marked by a single solid white line that turns into a dashed line near an intersection.

cites.quote: Typically marked by a single solid white line that turns into a dash-line near an intersection.

facts.text: A buffered bike lane uses chevrons or diagonal markings to give more separation from traffic and on-street parking.

cites.quote: Buffered bike lane: Uses chevrons or diagonal markings to provide greater separation from traffic and on-street parking.

facts.text: A bike route uses bike route signs and shared road markings to show a preferred route for bicyclists on streets shared with vehicle traffic.

cites.quote: Bike route: Uses bike route signs and shared road markings to designate a preferred route for bicyclists on streets shared with vehicle traffic.

facts.text: A bicycle boulevard prioritizes bicycle travel on streets shared with vehicle traffic.

cites.quote: Bicycle boulevard: Prioritizes bicycle travel on streets shared with vehicle traffic.

facts.text: A separated bikeway (cycle track or protected bike lane) is physically separated from motor vehicle traffic and is for the exclusive use of bicyclists.

cites.quote: Separated bikeway: Is physically separated from motor vehicle traffic and for exclusive use of bicyclists. They are also known as a cycle track or protected bike lanes.

facts.text: Shared roadway bicycle markings alert drivers that bicyclists can occupy the lane and help bicyclists keep a safe lane position.

cites.quote: Shared roadway bicycle markings: Alert drivers that bicyclists can occupy the lane and help bicyclists maintain a safe lane position in traffic.

facts.text: Check your blind spots before entering a bike lane.

cites.quote: Check your blind spots before entering a bike lane.

facts.text: If you ride a motorized bicycle, use caution to avoid other bicyclists, travel at a reasonable speed, and do not endanger other bicyclists.

cites.quote: If you drive a motorized bicycle, use caution to avoid other bicyclists. Travel at a reasonable speed and do not endanger the safety of other bicyclists.

facts.text: To make a right turn, drive close to the right edge of the road, entering a designated right turn lane at its opening if there is one.

cites.quote: To make a right turn:
Drive close to the right edge of the road.
If a designated right turn lane is available, enter at the opening.

facts.text: When preparing for a right turn, you may drive in a bike lane within 200 feet of the turn, checking for bicyclists in your blind spots.

cites.quote: You can drive in a bike lane within 200 feet from the turn. Check for bicyclists in your blind spots.

facts.text: When turning right, watch for pedestrians, bicyclists, or motorcyclists between your vehicle and the curb.

cites.quote: To make a right turn:
Watch for pedestrians, bicyclists, or motorcyclists between your vehicle and the curb.

facts.text: When making a right turn, start signaling about 100 feet before the turn.

cites.quote: To make a right turn:
Start signaling about 100 feet before the turn.

facts.text: When making a right turn, look over your right shoulder and reduce your speed.

cites.quote: To make a right turn:
Look over your right shoulder and reduce your speed.

facts.text: A limit line is a wide white line that shows drivers where to stop before an intersection or crosswalk.

cites.quote: A limit line is a wide white line that shows the drivers where to stop before an intersection or crosswalk.

facts.text: Stop behind the limit line; if there is no limit line, stop before the crosswalk; if there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

cites.quote: Stop behind the limit line.
If there is no limit line, stop before you enter the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before you enter the intersection.

facts.text: Before turning at an intersection, look both ways (left-right-left) and turn when it is safe.

cites.quote: Look both ways (left-right-left) and turn when it is safe.

facts.text: Complete a right turn in the right lane; do not turn wide into another lane.

cites.quote: Complete your turn in the right lane. Do not turn wide into another lane.

facts.text: You may turn right at a red light after a complete stop unless a No Turn on Red sign is posted.

cites.quote: You may turn right at a red light after a complete stop unless there is a No Turn on Red sign.

facts.text: You may not turn right while stopped at a red arrow; wait until the light turns green.

cites.quote: You may not turn right if you are stopped at a red arrow light. Wait until the light changes to green before making your turn.

facts.text: It is illegal to drive, stop, park, or leave a vehicle in an area designated for public transit buses.

cites.quote: It is illegal to drive, stop, park, or leave a vehicle in an area designated for public transit buses.

facts.text: You may cross a public transit bus lane to make a right turn.

cites.quote: However, you may cross a bus lane to make a right turn.

facts.text: A dedicated right turn lane does not merge into another lane and lets you turn right without stopping, even if the light is red for traffic going straight.

cites.quote: A dedicated right turn lane does not merge into another lane and allows you to make a right turn without stopping. You may make your turn even if there is a red light for vehicles going straight through the intersection.

facts.text: If there is a traffic light or sign on the right curb of a dedicated right turn lane, you must obey it.

cites.quote: If there is a traffic light or sign on the right curb of the right turn lane, you must obey that light or sign.

facts.text: Always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk when turning.

cites.quote: Always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk when turning.

facts.text: To turn left, drive close to the center divider or into the left turn lane, entering a designated left turn lane at its opening without crossing any solid line.

cites.quote: To turn left:
Drive close to the center divider or into the left turn lane.
Enter a designated left turn lane at the opening. Do not cross any solid line.

facts.text: When turning left, enter a two-way center left turn lane within 200 feet of the turn, respecting the right-of-way of anyone already in the lane and always yielding to pedestrians.

cites.quote: Enter a two-way center left turn lane within 200 feet of the turn. Respect the right-of-way of any vehicle, bicyclist, or motorcyclist already in the lane. Always yield to pedestrians.

facts.text: When turning left, start signaling 100 feet before the turn.

cites.quote: To turn left:
Start signaling 100 feet before the turn.

facts.text: When turning left, look over your left shoulder and reduce your speed.

cites.quote: To turn left:
Look over your left shoulder and reduce your speed.

facts.text: When turning left, proceed into the intersection while turning so that you complete the turn in the left lane.

cites.quote: Proceed into the intersection while turning to complete your turn in the left lane.

facts.text: While waiting to turn left, keep your wheels pointed straight ahead until it is safe to turn; if your wheels are turned left and you are hit from behind, you could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

cites.quote: Do not turn the steering wheel too soon and enter the lane of oncoming vehicles.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead until it is safe to start your turn. If your wheels are pointed to the left and a vehicle hits you from behind, you could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

facts.text: Accelerate smoothly during and after a left turn and let the steering wheel straighten in the new lane.

cites.quote: Accelerate smoothly during and after the turn.
Allow the steering wheel to straighten in the new lane.

facts.text: You may turn left against a red light when turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street, if no sign prohibits it, after yielding to vehicles, pedestrians, or bicyclists who have a green light.

cites.quote: You may turn left against a red light when you are turning from a one-way street onto a one-way street. Make sure there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Yield to other vehicles, pedestrians, or bicyclists who have a green light.

facts.text: To make a U-turn, signal and use the left turn lane or far-left lane.

cites.quote: To make a U-turn, signal and use the left turn lane or far-left lane.

facts.text: You may make a U-turn across a double yellow line.

cites.quote: You may make a U-turn:
Across a double yellow line.

facts.text: You may make a U-turn in a residential district if no vehicles are approaching within 200 feet.

cites.quote: You may make a U-turn:
In a residential district if no vehicles are approaching you within 200 feet.

facts.text: You may make a U-turn at an intersection on a green light or green arrow, unless a NO U-TURN sign is posted.

cites.quote: You may make a U-turn:
At an intersection on a green traffic light or green arrow, unless a NO U-TURN sign is posted.

facts.text: You may make a U-turn on a divided highway if a center divider opening is provided.

cites.quote: You may make a U-turn:
On a divided highway if a center divider opening is provided.

facts.text: Never make a U-turn where a NO U-TURN sign is posted.

cites.quote: Never make a U-turn:
Where a NO U-TURN sign is posted.

facts.text: Never make a U-turn at or on a railroad crossing.

cites.quote: Never make a U-turn:
At or on a railroad crossing.

facts.text: Never make a U-turn on a divided highway by crossing a dividing section, curb, strip of land, or two sets of double yellow lines.

cites.quote: Never make a U-turn:
On a divided highway by crossing a dividing section, curb, strip of land, or two sets of double yellow lines.

facts.text: Never make a U-turn when you cannot see clearly for 200 feet in each direction.

cites.quote: Never make a U-turn:
When you cannot see clearly for 200 feet in each direction.

facts.text: Never make a U-turn on a one-way street.

cites.quote: Never make a U-turn:
On a one-way street.

facts.text: Never make a U-turn in front of a fire station, and never use a fire station driveway to turn around.

cites.quote: Never make a U-turn:
In front of a fire station. Never use a fire station driveway to turn around.

facts.text: Never make a U-turn in a business district, except at an intersection or where a divided highway has an opening.

cites.quote: Never make a U-turn:
In business districts (the part of a city or town where most offices and businesses are).
Except at an intersection, or on a divided highway where an opening has been provided.

facts.text: A business district is the part of a city or town where most offices and businesses are.

cites.quote: the part of a city or town where most offices and businesses are

facts.text: When making turns, signs or arrows may show that you can turn from or end in more than one lane.

cites.quote: When making turns, there may be signs or arrows that indicate you can turn from or end in more than one lane.

facts.text: When turning left from a two-way street, start in the left lane closest to the middle of the street and end in the left lane closest to the middle of the street going your direction.

cites.quote: Left turn from a two-way street. Start the turn in the left lane closest to the middle of the street. To reduce the risk of collision, end the turn in the left lane closest to the middle of the street going in your vehicle’s direction.

facts.text: For a right turn, begin and end in the lane closest to the right edge of the road and do not swing wide into another lane.

cites.quote: Right turn. Begin and end the turn in the lane closest to the right edge of the road. Do not swing wide into another lane of traffic.

facts.text: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, start from the lane closest to the middle (far-left lane); if there are three or more lanes in your direction, you may end in any open lane.

cites.quote: Left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Start the turn from the lane closest to the middle of the street (far-left lane). If there are three or more lanes in your direction of travel, you may end your turn in any lane that is open.

facts.text: When turning left from a one-way street onto a two-way street, start from the far-left lane and end in the left lane closest to the middle of the street going your direction.

cites.quote: Left turn from a one-way street onto a two-way street. Start the turn from the far-left lane. To reduce the risk of collision, end the turn in the left lane closest to the middle of the street going in your vehicle’s direction.

facts.text: When turning left from a one-way street onto a one-way street, start from the far-left lane; if there are three or more lanes in your direction, you may end in any open lane.

cites.quote: Left turn from a one-way street onto a one-way street. Start the turn from the far-left lane.
If there are three or more lanes in your direction of travel, you may end your turn in any lane that is open.

facts.text: Bicyclists can legally use the left turn lane for their left turns.

cites.quote: Bicyclists can legally use the left turn lane for their left turns.

facts.text: When turning right from a one-way street onto a one-way street, start in the far-right lane; if safe, you may end in any lane.

cites.quote: Right turn from a one-way street onto a one-way street. Start the turn in the far-right lane. If safe, you may end the turn in any lane.

facts.text: At a T intersection from a one-way street onto a two-way street, traffic going straight through has the right-of-way, and you may turn right or left from the center lane.

cites.quote: Turn at a “T” intersection from a one-way street onto a two-way street. Traffic going straight through the intersection has the right-of-way. You may turn either right or left from the center lane.

facts.text: To brake, take your foot off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow, then lightly press the brake until you stop, giving yourself enough space and time.

cites.quote: Remove your foot from the accelerator and allow the vehicle to slow down. Lightly press the brake until you come to a full stop. Give yourself enough space and time to perform this maneuver.

facts.text: When stopping at a limit line, do not cross over the line.

cites.quote: When stopping at a limit line, do not cross over the line.

facts.text: When stopping behind another vehicle, leave enough space to see its rear wheels.

cites.quote: If stopping behind a vehicle, leave enough space to see their rear wheels.

facts.text: When entering a highway, highway traffic has the right-of-way.

cites.quote: Highway traffic has the right-of-way.

facts.text: When entering a highway, be in the proper lane on the on-ramp and be at or near the speed of traffic.

cites.quote: When you enter a highway, you will need to:
Be in the proper lane on the on-ramp.
Be at or near the speed of traffic.

facts.text: When entering a highway, merge when it is safe and do not stop unless absolutely necessary.

cites.quote: Merge into highway traffic when safe to do so. Do not stop unless absolutely necessary.

facts.text: When entering a highway, merge into a space large enough for your vehicle to join the lane safely.

cites.quote: Merge into a space large enough for your vehicle to safely join the lane.

facts.text: When merging, use your mirrors and turn signals, and quickly look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

cites.quote: Use your mirrors and turn signals.
Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging into traffic.

facts.text: After merging onto a highway, leave three seconds of space between you and the vehicle ahead so you can stop safely.

cites.quote: Make sure you can stop safely by leaving three seconds of space between you and the vehicle in front of you.

facts.text: Do not cross any solid lines when merging.

cites.quote: Make sure you do not cross over any solid lines when merging.

facts.text: If you need to cross several lanes, signal and cross them one at a time, checking your blind spots each time.

cites.quote: If you need to cross several lanes, signal and cross them one at a time. Check your blind spots for vehicles, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians each time.

facts.text: To exit a highway safely, know your exit and be aware of when it is approaching.

cites.quote: To exit a highway safely:
Know your exit and be aware of when it is approaching.

facts.text: When preparing to exit a highway, change lanes one at a time, signaling and looking over your shoulder to check blind spots.

cites.quote: If you plan to change lanes, do so one at a time. Signal and look over your shoulder to check your blind spots.

facts.text: When you are in the proper lane, signal five seconds (about 400 feet) before you exit a highway.

cites.quote: When in the proper lane, signal five seconds (approximately 400 feet) before you exit.

facts.text: Make sure you are at a safe speed to exit a highway.

cites.quote: Make sure you are at a safe speed to exit.

facts.text: Do not cross any solid lines when exiting a highway.

cites.quote: Do not cross over any solid lines when exiting.

facts.text: When entering traffic from a full stop, signal and leave a space large enough to get up to the speed of traffic.

cites.quote: When entering traffic from a full stop, signal and leave a large enough space to get up to the speed of traffic.

facts.text: To merge, enter, or exit traffic on city streets, you need a gap of about half a block, about 150 feet.

cites.quote: To merge, enter, or exit traffic, you need a space that is:
Half a block on city streets, which is about 150 feet.

facts.text: To merge, enter, or exit traffic on the highway, you need a gap of about a full block, about 300 feet.

cites.quote: To merge, enter, or exit traffic, you need a space that is:
A full block on the highway, which is about 300 feet.

facts.text: Even with a green light, do not start across an intersection if pedestrians or vehicles are blocking your path.

cites.quote: Even if you have a green light, do not start across the intersection if there are pedestrians or vehicles blocking your pathway.

facts.text: When turning left, do not assume an oncoming vehicle with its right signal on will turn before reaching you; wait for it to start its turn.

cites.quote: When turning left, do not assume that an oncoming vehicle with its right turn signal on is turning before it reaches you.
Wait for the vehicle to start its turn before beginning the left turn.

facts.text: Judge whether you have enough space to pass whenever you approach an oncoming vehicle or bicyclist, or a hill, curve, intersection, or road obstruction.

cites.quote: You must judge whether you have enough space to pass whenever you approach:
An oncoming vehicle or bicyclist.
A hill, curve, intersection, or road obstruction.

facts.text: To pass safely, a hill or curve ahead should be at least one-third of a mile away.

cites.quote: To safely pass, the hill or curve should be at least one-third of a mile ahead.

facts.text: Before you pass, look ahead for road conditions that may cause other vehicles to move into your lane.

cites.quote: Before you pass, look ahead for road conditions that may cause other vehicles to move into your lane.

facts.text: Do not pass when approaching a hill or curve if you cannot see whether traffic is coming; this is very dangerous on one- and two-lane roads.

cites.quote: Do not pass:
If you are approaching a hill or curve and cannot see if other traffic is approaching. This is very dangerous on one and two lane roads.

facts.text: Do not pass within 100 feet of an intersection, bridge, tunnel, railroad crossing, or other hazardous area.

cites.quote: Do not pass:
Within 100 feet of an intersection, bridge, tunnel, railroad crossing, or other hazardous area.

facts.text: Do not pass at crossroads and driveways.

cites.quote: Do not pass:
At crossroads and driveways.

facts.text: Do not pass unless you have enough space to return to your lane.

cites.quote: Do not pass:
Unless you have enough space to return to your lane.

facts.text: To pass on an open highway, signal, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, move into the passing lane, speed up to pass, then signal and return to your original lane.

cites.quote: When you are going to pass on an open highway:
Signal that you plan on passing.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spots.
Drive into the passing lane.
Speed up to pass the vehicle.
Signal and return to your original lane.

facts.text: You may pass on the right on an open highway with two or more lanes going your direction.

cites.quote: You may pass on the right only when:
An open highway has two or more lanes going in your direction.

facts.text: You may pass on the right when the driver ahead is turning left and you can do so safely.

cites.quote: You may pass on the right only when:
The driver ahead of you is turning left and you can safely pass on the right.

facts.text: Never pass on the left if the driver ahead is signaling a left turn.

cites.quote: Never pass on the left if the driver is signaling a left turn.

facts.text: You may pass on the right on a one-way street.

cites.quote: You may pass on the right only when:
You are on a one-way street.

facts.text: Never drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass.

cites.quote: Never drive off the paved or main-traveled part of the road to pass.

facts.text: If a vehicle is passing you or signals that it plans to pass, let it pass and keep your lane position and speed.

cites.quote: If a vehicle is passing you or signals that they plan on passing, allow the vehicle to pass. Maintain your lane position and your speed.

facts.text: Parallel parking is parking in line with the road and other parked vehicles.

cites.quote: Parallel parking is when you park in line with the road and other parked vehicles.

facts.text: For parallel parking, look for a space at least three feet longer than your vehicle and turn on your signal when you find one.

cites.quote: Look for a space at least three feet longer than your vehicle. When you find a space, turn on your signal to show that you plan on parking.

facts.text: To parallel park, pull up alongside the vehicle in front of the space, leaving about two feet between the vehicles, and stop when your rear bumper lines up with the front of the space.

cites.quote: Pull up alongside the vehicle in front of the space. Leave about two feet between your vehicle and the vehicle next to you. Stop once your rear bumper is aligned with the front of your parking space.

facts.text: Before backing into a parallel parking space, check your blind spots by looking in your rearview mirror and over your shoulder for vehicles and pedestrians.

cites.quote: Check your blind spots. Look in your rearview mirror and over your shoulder for approaching vehicles and pedestrians.

facts.text: When parallel parking, back into the space at about a 45-degree angle.

cites.quote: Turn your steering wheel to back into the space at about a 45-degree angle.

facts.text: When parallel parking, start turning the wheel away from the curb when your rear wheel is within 18 inches of the curb; the vehicle should end parallel and within 18 inches of the curb.

cites.quote: Begin turning the steering wheel away from the curb when your rear wheel is within 18 inches of the curb.
Your vehicle should now be parallel and within 18 inches of the curb.

facts.text: After parking, turn off the vehicle, set the parking brake, and look carefully for passing vehicles, bicycles, and motorcycles before getting out.

cites.quote: Turn off your vehicle and set the parking brake. Before you exit your vehicle, look carefully for passing vehicles, bicycles, and motorcycles.

facts.text: When backing in a straight line, back for three vehicle lengths while staying within three feet of the curb, staying aware of what is behind you.

cites.quote: Back in a straight line for three vehicle lengths while remaining within three feet of the curb. Stay aware of what is behind you when backing up.

facts.text: Before backing in a straight line, observe traffic and check your blind spots, using your rearview mirror and looking over your shoulder.

cites.quote: Observe traffic and check appropriate blind spots.
Look in your rearview mirror and over your shoulder for approaching vehicles and pedestrians.

facts.text: When backing, go at a smooth, safe speed and adjust the steering wheel when needed to keep control.

cites.quote: To maintain control of the vehicle, back at a smooth, safe speed and adjust the steering wheel when needed.

facts.text: When parking on a hill, set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park (or in gear for a manual transmission), because equipment failure could let it roll.

cites.quote: When you park on a hill, your vehicle could roll due to equipment failure. Remember to set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in park, or in gear for manual transmission.

facts.text: On a sloping driveway, turn the wheels so the vehicle will not roll into the street, leave it in park, and set the parking brake.

cites.quote: On a sloping driveway: Turn the wheels so the vehicle will not roll into the street, leave the vehicle in park and set the parking brake.

facts.text: When parking headed downhill, turn your front wheels into the curb or right toward the side of the road.

cites.quote: Headed downhill: Turn your front wheels into the curb or right toward the side of the road.

facts.text: When parking headed uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb (left, toward the center of the road) and let the vehicle roll back a few inches so the wheel gently touches the curb.

cites.quote: Headed uphill: Turn your front wheels away from the curb (left-towards the center of the road) and let your vehicle roll back a few inches. The wheel should gently touch the curb.

facts.text: When parking uphill or downhill with no curb, turn the wheels to the right so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail.

cites.quote: Headed either uphill or downhill when there is no curb: Turn the wheels to the right so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail.

facts.text: A white curb means stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers.

cites.quote: White : Stop only long enough to pick up or drop off passengers.

facts.text: A green curb means you may park for a limited time, posted on signs or painted on the curb.

cites.quote: Green : Park for a limited time. The time limit may be posted on signs or painted on the curb.

facts.text: A yellow curb is for loading and unloading passengers and freight, for no longer than the posted time.

cites.quote: Yellow : Load and unload passengers and freight. Do not stop longer than the time posted.

facts.text: At a yellow curb, drivers of noncommercial vehicles are usually required to stay with their vehicle.

cites.quote: If you drive a noncommercial vehicle, you are usually required to stay with your vehicle.

facts.text: A red curb means no stopping, standing, or parking; buses may stop at a red zone marked for buses only.

cites.quote: Red : No stopping, standing, or parking. Buses may stop at a red zone marked for buses only.

facts.text: A blue curb is parking for a disabled person, or someone driving a disabled person, with a special placard or license plate.

cites.quote: Blue : Parking for a disabled person or someone driving a disabled person with a special placard or special license plate.

facts.text: Never park where a NO PARKING sign is posted.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
Where a NO PARKING sign is posted.

facts.text: Never park on a marked or unmarked crosswalk.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
On a marked or unmarked crosswalk.

facts.text: Never park on a sidewalk, partially blocking a sidewalk, or in front of a driveway.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
On a sidewalk, partially blocking a sidewalk, or in front of a driveway.

facts.text: Never park within three feet of a sidewalk ramp for disabled persons.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
Within three feet of a sidewalk ramp for disabled persons.

facts.text: Never park in front of or on a curb that provides wheelchair access to a sidewalk.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
In front of or on a curb that provides wheelchair access to a sidewalk.

facts.text: Never park in the crosshatched (diagonal lines) area next to a designated disabled parking space.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
In the crosshatched (diagonal lines) area next to a designated disabled parking space.

facts.text: Never park in a space designated for parking or fueling zero-emission vehicles unless you are driving a zero-emission vehicle.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
In a space designated for parking or fueling zero-emission vehicles, unless you are driving a zero-emission vehicle.

facts.text: Never park in a tunnel or on a bridge unless signs permit it.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
In a tunnel or on a bridge, unless permitted by signs.

facts.text: Never park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or a fire station driveway.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant or fire station driveway.

facts.text: Never park within 20 feet of a marked or unmarked crosswalk, or within 15 feet of a crosswalk where there is a curb extension.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
Within 20 feet of an unmarked or marked crosswalk, or within 15 feet of a crosswalk where a curb extension is present.

facts.text: Never park between a safety zone and the curb.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
Between a safety zone and curb.

facts.text: Never double park.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
Double parked.

facts.text: Never park on the wrong side of the street or on a freeway, except in an emergency, when a law enforcement officer requires a stop, or where a stop is specifically permitted.

cites.quote: Never park or leave your vehicle:
On the wrong side of the street or on a freeway, except:
In an emergency.
When a law enforcement officer requires a stop.
Where a stop is specifically permitted.

facts.text: If you must stop on a freeway, park completely off the pavement and stay in your vehicle with the doors locked until help arrives.

cites.quote: If you must stop on a freeway, park completely off the pavement and stay in your vehicle with the doors locked until help arrives.

facts.text: A vehicle stopped, parked, or left standing on a freeway for more than four hours may be removed.

cites.quote: A vehicle that is stopped, parked, or left standing on a freeway for more than four hours may be removed.

facts.text: Local authorities can reserve parking spaces on public streets for electric vehicle charging.

cites.quote: Local authorities can reserve parking spaces on public streets for electric vehicle charging.

facts.text: To maximize fuel efficiency and lower emissions, speed up and slow down smoothly and drive at a steady speed.

cites.quote: Maximize your fuel efficiency while helping to lower emissions
Speed up and slow down smoothly. Drive at a steady speed.

facts.text: To maximize fuel efficiency, regularly inflate your tires, get oil changes, and check filters.

cites.quote: Maximize your fuel efficiency
Regularly inflate your tires, get oil changes, and check filters.

facts.text: To maximize fuel efficiency, get rid of extra weight in your vehicle.

cites.quote: Maximize your fuel efficiency
Get rid of extra weight in your vehicle.

facts.text: When stopped by law enforcement, turn on your right turn signal to show you see the officer.

cites.quote: Turn on your right turn signal to acknowledge that you see the officer.

facts.text: During a law enforcement stop, move completely onto the right shoulder, even if you are in the carpool/HOV lane, and stop in a well-lit area when possible.

cites.quote: Move completely onto the right shoulder, even if in the carpool/HOV lane. Stop in a well-lit area when possible.

facts.text: During a law enforcement stop, turn off your radio.

cites.quote: Turn off your radio.

facts.text: During a law enforcement stop, stay inside your vehicle unless the officer directs you to get out.

cites.quote: Remain inside your vehicle unless directed to get out by the officer.

facts.text: During a law enforcement stop, roll down your window after stopping and before the officer reaches you.

cites.quote: Roll down your window after stopping your vehicle and before the officer makes contact with you.

facts.text: During a law enforcement stop, the driver and all passengers should place their hands in clear view before the officer makes contact.

cites.quote: The driver and all passengers should place their hands in clear view before the officer makes contact with them.

facts.text: Law enforcement officers must state the reason for a traffic or pedestrian stop before questioning you about a criminal investigation or traffic violation, unless withholding it is reasonably necessary to protect life or property from imminent threat.

cites.quote: Law enforcement officers must state the reason for a traffic or pedestrian stop before they begin any questioning related to a criminal investigation or traffic violation. An exception is made if an officer reasonably believes withholding the reason is necessary to protect life or property from imminent threat.

facts.text: The reason for a stop must be documented on the traffic citation (ticket) or law enforcement report.

cites.quote: The reason for the stop must be documented on the traffic citation also known as a traffic ticket issued or law enforcement report completed.

facts.text: If an officer asks permission to do something, you may say no, but if the officer proceeds anyway you have no right to interfere.

cites.quote: If an officer asks your permission to do something, you have a right to say no. However, if you say no and the officer says they are going to do it anyway, you do not have a right to interfere with their actions.

facts.text: You may decline an officer's request to search your vehicle by clearly saying you do not give permission, but you may not resist or obstruct the officer if they search it.

cites.quote: If you do not want the officer to search your vehicle, you should clearly say that you do not give your permission, but you do not have a right to resist or obstruct the officer if they search your vehicle.

facts.text: When stopped by law enforcement, the driver must produce a driver's license, proof of insurance, and vehicle registration.

cites.quote: The driver of a stopped vehicle must produce a driver’s license, proof of insurance, and vehicle registration when stopped by law enforcement.

facts.text: If a stopped driver does not produce their license, insurance, and registration, officers may conduct a limited search for them.

cites.quote: If a driver does not produce these documents, officers may conduct a limited search for them.

facts.text: Passengers may decline an officer's request for identification, but in some circumstances they may be required to identify themselves, and they should not interfere with the officer.

cites.quote: Passengers can decline that request, but under some circumstances the passengers may be required to identify themselves.
Passengers should not interfere with the officer’s duties in conducting the traffic stop

facts.text: During a traffic stop, an officer can legally require the driver and all passengers to exit or stay in the vehicle, and you must comply.

cites.quote: During a traffic stop, an officer can legally require the driver and all passengers to exit or stay inside the vehicle. If you are told to exit the vehicle or stay inside, you must do so.

facts.text: In California, only federal law enforcement officers can ask about your immigration status; state and local officers are prohibited from asking, and you can decline to answer.

cites.quote: In California, only federal law enforcement officers can ask you about your immigration status. California law prohibits state and local officers from asking drivers or passengers about their immigration status. If a California law enforcement officer asks you about your immigration status, you can decline to answer.

facts.text: Drivers and passengers generally have a First Amendment right to record interactions with law enforcement in public, and should immediately make it clear that they are recording.

cites.quote: In general, the First Amendment protects the right of drivers and passengers to record interactions with law enforcement in public spaces. If you are recording, you should immediately make that clear.

facts.text: While recording a stop, do not interfere with the officer's lawful duties or reach into concealed areas for your recording device without permission.

cites.quote: You do not have a right to interfere with the officer’s lawful duties during the enforcement stop, and you should not reach into concealed areas to retrieve your recording device without the officer’s permission.

facts.text: If your recording does not interfere with the officer's lawful duties, the officer cannot confiscate your device, delete the recording, or destroy the device just because you are recording.

cites.quote: If your recording is not interfering with the officer’s ability to lawfully do their job, an officer cannot confiscate your recording device, delete the recording, or destroy the device just because you are using it to record.

facts.text: You generally have the right to refuse to unlock your phone or give its password, though in some circumstances, such as being on parole, you may have to.

cites.quote: In general, you also have the right to deny a request to unlock a cellular phone or provide a password to it, though under some circumstances, such as if you are on parole, you may have to give permission in response to such requests.

facts.text: No government employee can retaliate against you just because you recorded something in public.

cites.quote: no government employee can retaliate against you just because you recorded something in public.

facts.text: Even if you believe an officer violated your rights, do not physically resist or use violence; you may voice your objection.

cites.quote: Even if you believe your rights were violated, you should not engage in physical resistance or violence against the officer. If an officer does something that you believe violates your rights, you can voice your objection, but you should not physically resist.

facts.text: Anyone may file a complaint with the agency that employs an officer, the agency must investigate it, and it is illegal for a government employee to retaliate against you for filing.

cites.quote: All members of the public have a right to file a complaint against any law enforcement agency, and it is against the law for any government employee to retaliate against you for doing so. You can file a complaint with the law enforcement agency that employs the officer.
When you file a complaint, the agency that employs the officer must investigate the complaint.

facts.text: You have a right to be free from discrimination during a stop based on actual or perceived race, sex, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability, medical condition, or citizenship status.

cites.quote: You have a right to be free from discrimination based on your actual or perceived race, sex, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, mental or physical disability, medical condition, or citizenship status.
